lootbeams.title: Loot Beams
lootbeams.config.main.renderNameColor.de:
If beams should be colored the same as the Items name (excludes name colors from rarity). 
This has priority over render_rarity_color.
If beams should be colored the same as the Items rarity.
lootbeams.config.main.renderBeam.descrip: If Loot beam should be visible.
lootbeams.config.main.renderDroplightBea: If Loot beam should be like droplight.
lootbeams.config.main.animateDroplightBe: If Loot beam should be animated.
lootbeams.config.main.beamGradientModifi: Modifiers to be applied to color to get second gradient color.
lootbeams.config.main.smoothBeamSize.des: If Loot beam side should change smooth.
lootbeams.config.main.beamRadius.descrip: The radius of the Loot Beam.
lootbeams.config.main.minBeamRadius.desc: The minimal radius of the Loot Beam.
lootbeams.config.main.beamHeight.descrip: The height of the Loot Beam.
lootbeams.config.main.minBeamHeight.desc: The minimal height of the Loot Beam.
lootbeams.config.main.beamYOffset.descri: The height of the Loot Beam.
If the Loot Beam should be shorter for common items.
lootbeams.config.main.minBeamAlpha.descr: Minimal transparency of the Loot Beam.
lootbeams.config.main.solidBeam.descript: If the Loot Beam should use a solid texture or the beacon style texture.
lootbeams.config.main.whiteCenter.descri: If the Loot Beam should have a white center.
lootbeams.config.main.glowingBeam.descri: If the Loot Beam should be glowing.
lootbeams.config.main.renderDistance.des:
How close the player has to be to see the beam.
(note: this option overwrite default Item render distance)
lootbeams.config.main.changeDistance.des:
How close the player has to be to the beam to cause beam changes.
 (note: smooth distance is 1 unit)
lootbeams.config.main.changeOffset.descr: Distance from beam (in blocks) when beam changes starts.
lootbeams.config.main.beamOpacityOnAppro: Enables or disables the fading effect of the loot beam when an player approaches it.
lootbeams.config.main.beamSizeOnApproach: Enables or disables the size change of the loot beam when an player approaches it.
lootbeams.config.main.requireOnGround.de: If the item must be on the ground to render a beam.
lootbeams.config.groundGlow.glowEffect.d: If the Loot Beam should have a glow effect around the base of the item.
lootbeams.config.groundGlow.glowCustomSh: If the Ground Effect should use a custom shader.
lootbeams.config.groundGlow.useGlowGradi: If the Ground Effect should use a gradient color.
lootbeams.config.groundGlow.glowGradient: Modifiers to be applied to color to get second gradient color.
The position in percentage where the gradient should start transitioning the color.
The position in percentage where the gradient should end transitioning the color.
lootbeams.config.groundGlow.smoothGlowEf: If the Ground Effect should change it's radius smooth.
If the Ground Effect should change it's alpha smooth.
lootbeams.config.groundGlow.glowEffectTe: Glow Effect texture in format "lootbeams:effect_id" where effect_id is effect image file name without extension. (assets/lootbeams/textures/ground_glow_effects) - path to dir in resource pack.
lootbeams.config.groundGlow.glowEffectRa: The radius of the glow effect.
lootbeams.config.groundGlow.pulseGlow.de: If the glow effect should pulse.
lootbeams.config.groundGlow.pulseGlowMin: Minimal glow effect alpha when pulsating.
lootbeams.config.groundGlow.pulseGlowMax: Maximal glow effect alpha when pulsating.
lootbeams.config.groundGlow.pulseGlowMin: Minimal radius of glow effect when pulsating.
lootbeams.config.groundGlow.pulseGlowMax: Maximal radius of glow effect when pulsating.
lootbeams.config.groundGlow.rotateGlow.d: If the glow effect should rotate.
lootbeams.config.groundGlow.glowRotateCl: If the glow effect should rotate clockwise.
lootbeams.config.particles.particles.des: If particles should appear around the item.
lootbeams.config.particles.particleTextu: Particle texture in format "lootbeams:particle_id" where particle_id is particle image file name without extension. (assets/lootbeams/textures/particle) - path to dir in resource pack.
lootbeams.config.particles.particleColor: What function particles should use when blending the beam color with the texture
lootbeams.config.particles.particleInher: Should the particles inherit color from the beam ("false" can be useful in cases where the particle texture is multicolored)
lootbeams.config.particles.tickPerPartic: How many ticks pass before sprite update (only for splitted sprites)
lootbeams.config.particles.particleRando: Should particle have a small random Y offset when spawn.
Should particle have a random size close to Particle Size.
lootbeams.config.particles.particleSpeed: The speed of the particles by X axis.
The speed of the particles by Y axis.
The speed of the particles by Z axis.
lootbeams.config.particles.particleUseCo: If particles should use constant axis speed.
lootbeams.config.particles.randomnessInt: The intensity of the randomness of the particles.
lootbeams.config.particles.particleCount: The amount of particles to spawn per second.
lootbeams.config.particles.particleLifet: The lifetime of the particles in ticks.
lootbeams.config.particles.particleRareO: If particles should only appear on rare items.
lootbeams.config.particles.particleDirec: The direction of the particles on the X axis.
The direction of the particles on the Y axis.
The direction of the particles on the Z axis.
lootbeams.config.particles.spinAroundBea: If the particles should spin around the beam.
lootbeams.config.particles.trails.descri: If the particles should leave a trail.
lootbeams.config.particles.trailParticle: If the particles with a trail should be invisible.
lootbeams.config.particles.trailUseScale: If the trails should use Y scaling.
lootbeams.config.particles.trailScaleHei: Trail Scale Height Equals Beam Height
If the trail scale height should be equal to beam height.
What height should be used if trail uses scale and it's not equal to beam height
lootbeams.config.particles.trailChance.d: The chance of a particle leaving a trail.
lootbeams.config.particles.trailFrequenc: The frequency of the trail. The maximum value this should be is the length. The lower the frequency, the smoother the trail.
lootbeams.config.items.allItems.descript:
If all Items Loot Beams should be rendered.
 Has priority over only_equipment and only_rare.
lootbeams.config.items.onlyRare.descript: If Loot Beams should only be rendered on items with rarity.
lootbeams.config.items.onlyEquipment.des:
If Loot Beams should only be rendered on equipment.
 (Equipment includes: Swords, Tools, Armor, Shields, Bows, Crossbows, Tridents, Arrows, and Fishing Rods)
lootbeams.config.items.whitelist.descrip:
Registry names of items that Loot Beams should render on.
 Example: "minecraft:stone", "minecraft:iron_ingot", 
You can also specify modids for a whole mod's items
lootbeams.config.items.blacklist.descrip:
Registry names of items that Loot Beams should NOT render on. This has priority over everything.
 You can also specify modids for a whole mod's items.
lootbeams.config.items.colorOverrides.de:
Overrides an item's beam color with hex color.
 Must follow the specific format: (registryname=hexcolor) Or (#tagname=hexcolor).
 Examples: "minecraft:stone=#00FF00", "#minecraft:piglin_loved=gold". This also accepts modids.
lootbeams.config.nametags.advancedToolti: If vanilla tooltips should be rendered on items in world.
lootbeams.config.nametags.itemFrameToolt: If vanilla tooltips should be rendered on item frames in world (only for items with custom name).
lootbeams.config.nametags.worldspaceTool: If tooltips should be rendered in world.
lootbeams.config.nametags.renderTooltips: If tooltips should be rendered in world when F5.
lootbeams.config.nametags.borders.descri: Render nametags as bordered. Set to false for flat nametag with background.
lootbeams.config.nametags.renderNametags: If Item nametags should be rendered at all.
If Item nametags should be rendered when looking at items.
lootbeams.config.nametags.renderItemRari: If Item rarity should be rendered at all.
If Item rarity should be rendered in item tooltip.
lootbeams.config.nametags.renderStackcou: If the count of item's should also be shown in the nametag.
lootbeams.config.nametags.nametagLookSen: How close the player has to look at the item to render the nametag.
lootbeams.config.nametags.dmclootCompatR: If a smaller tag should be rendered under with DMCLoot rarities.
lootbeams.config.nametags.customRarities:
Define what the smaller tag should render on. 
Example: "Exotic", "Ancient". 
The string supplied has to be the tooltip line below the name. 
This is really only used for modpacks.
lootbeams.config.nametags.alwaysDrawRari:
Define on which items smaller tag should render on. 
Example: "#minecraft:music_discs" will render song name as smaller tag. 
Be aware that text rendered is a tooltip line below the name so it wont work well with multiple enchantments (though 1 enchantment looks pretty good)
If rarities should ignore color and render as white 
(This is really only used for modpacks)
lootbeams.config.nametags.vanillaRaritie: If vanilla rarities should be rendered.
lootbeams.config.nametags.screenTooltips: If the player should be crouching to see extended advanced tooltips.
lootbeams.config.nametags.combineNameAnd: If the name and rarity should be combined into one tooltip.
